name: Black vertices pass through the crossing with a sign
summary: Moving a wire across a black vertex through fermionic crossings puts a weight −1 on it.
description:
The *crossing* (fermionic swap) of the ZW-calculus is the map $|00\rangle\langle 00| + |01\rangle\langle 10| + |10\rangle\langle 01| - |11\rangle\langle 11|$: a swap that picks up a sign $-1$ when two $|1\rangle$'s (two fermions) are exchanged. It equals a SWAP followed by a CZ. It behaves like a symmetric braiding, except that it is only natural for *even* maps (those whose terms all have an even number of 1s); maps of odd parity, such as the black vertices, pick up signs. 

The symmetric black vertex (the W-state $\sum_k |0\cdots010\cdots0\rangle$, drawn as a triangle without input dot) is *odd*: each of its terms has exactly one $|1\rangle$. So a wire that crosses all its legs on one side through fermionic crossings can be moved to cross all its legs on the other side, at the price of a weight $-1$ (the Pauli Z) on that wire.

Compare with [the W merge](../fermionic-crossing-w-merge/), which is even and passes the crossing without a sign.
parameter_notes: Shown for a black vertex with two legs on each side; holds for any number of legs.
unchecked_reason: uses the fermionic crossing of the ZW-calculus, which is not a PyZX generator
